## Proposed change: add a 16-word block between the main loop and the tail ladder

The current program is already a fully unrolled 16-word loop followed by a branch ladder for the remaining 0–15 words. Its cost is 3836 against a reference of 7570, and the three previous attempts with different leaf structures all scored exactly 2.9734, so restructuring the ladder alone is unlikely to help.

The change below targets the main loop's per-iteration overhead. After the 16-word loop, at most 15 words remain. Adding one `if len(xs) >= 16` block before the ladder lets the loop's loop-control work happen once per 16 words, while the ladder still handles any remainder of 0–15 words. Only the 16-word work is duplicated, so the ladder and its leaves are untouched.

I can't measure the instruction count here, so the gain is an estimate, not a verified result. I expect it to be small. For inputs whose length is 16 or more, the effect is one extra compare on the exit path. The benefit is that remainders of 16–31 words take a single pass through the big block instead of the ladder. Any inputs under 16 words pay one extra compare.
